title: Finite-level derived tensor has constructible cohomology without a boundedness claim
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and an integer $n\geq1$. Put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $T$ be a scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible. Work on the small pro-etale site $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] with the constant ring sheaf $A_T$. Let $K,L\in D^b_c(T,A)$ in the intrinsic finite-torsion sense of [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. For every integer $i$, the cohomology sheaf $\mathcal H^i(K\otimes_A^L L)$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves, def-weil-derived-tensor] is constructible in the sense of [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf]. No lower cohomological bound on this tensor product is asserted.

source.place: Tag 09BQ, lemma-tensor-c (specialized to bounded inputs and finite DVR quotient coefficients)

proof.text: The absolute value of $E$ is nonarchimedean by [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-absolute-value]. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], its valuation ring is a DVR with finite residue field, and the chosen uniformizer generates its maximal ideal. Apply [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients] with $K=E$ and $n\geq1$ to conclude that $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ is finite. In particular $A$ is Noetherian: every ideal is a finite set and is generated by its elements. A finitely generated $A$-module is finite as a set, since it is a quotient of $A^m$ for some finite $m$.

source.place: Coefficient datum; existing l-adic valuation and finite DVR quotient lemmas make its finite coefficient claim explicit

proof.text: Boundedness in [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] leaves only finitely many nonzero cohomology sheaves of $K$ and $L$. For each of these choose a witnessing finite stratification from [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf]. Starting with the trivial partition, apply [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-stratification-intersection] successively to each of the finitely many chosen partitions. Its statement supplies constructible locally closed intersection strata with iterated fibre-product scheme structures. The fibre-product projections give actual maps to the original strata; omit empty intersections when $T$ is nonempty. By [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], base change sends each original trivializing cover to a covering of the new stratum. On that cover the pulled-back sheaf is constant with the original module value: inverse image preserves constant sheaves because a constant set sheaf is the coproduct of copies of the terminal sheaf, and inverse image preserves coproducts and the terminal sheaf. Applying this identification to addition and the $A$-action gives the same constant module. Composed restrictions agree because iterated base-change functors agree by the fibre-product universal property, so their left adjoints agree by uniqueness of adjoints. Thus on this one finite partition $T=\bigsqcup_\alpha T_\alpha$ all the input cohomology sheaves restrict to locally constant sheaves with finite $A$-module stalks. If both inputs have zero cohomology, use the trivial partition with stratum $T$. If $T$ is empty, retain the single empty stratum $T$; the local constancy and finiteness conditions are vacuous.

source.place: Tag 095I, lemma-tensor-product-constructible: common stratification argument, applied to the finite list of input cohomology sheaves

proof.text:
Write $i_\alpha:T_\alpha\to T$ for each immersion. Use the constant-coefficient identification $i_\alpha^{-1}A_T\cong A_{T_\alpha}$ and the module pullback of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Inverse image is exact on abelian sheaves by [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact]. Kernels and cokernels of module sheaves have these underlying abelian sheaves, by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; transporting the action through the ring isomorphism is exact. Therefore module pullback is exact. On a representative complex it sends $\ker d^q/\operatorname{im}d^{q-1}$ to the corresponding quotient for the pulled-back differentials. Hence $\mathcal H^q(Li_\alpha^*C)=i_\alpha^*\mathcal H^q(C)$ for every complex $C$, and $Li_\alpha^*$ is the termwise inverse image. The canonical derived tensor comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], applied to these ringed pro-etale topoi, gives
$$Li_\alpha^*(K\otimes_A^L L)\cong Li_\alpha^*K\otimes_A^L Li_\alpha^*L.$$
Its hypotheses concern sites small relative to the module universe; the small pro-etale sites use precisely the size convention of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. In particular both pulled-back inputs remain bounded, and their cohomology sheaves are the locally constant finite sheaves of step 2.

source.place: Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product; exact identified-coefficient inverse image

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-locally-constant-tensor] on $(T_\alpha)_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with the Noetherian ring $B=A$ of step 1 and the bounded, hence bounded-above, inputs $Li_\alpha^*K,Li_\alpha^*L$ of step 3. Its statement asserts that every cohomology sheaf of their derived tensor is locally constant of finite type; it assumes neither finite Tor dimension nor a lower bound on the output. By step 1, finite type over $A$ implies finite stalks. For each integer $i$, the identifications in step 3 therefore show that $i_\alpha^*\mathcal H^i(K\otimes_A^L L)$ is locally constant with finite $A$-module stalks for every $\alpha$.

For any integer $i$, use the finite partition of step 2 and the local constancy and finite stalks established in step 4 in the definition [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf]. This is exactly a witnessing stratification for $\mathcal H^i(K\otimes_A^L L)$, so this sheaf is constructible. The same input partition works for every $i$, but the argument makes no claim that the tensor has only finitely many nonzero cohomology sheaves.
